#--------------------------- ABOUT THIS SCRIPT: ---------------------------#

title: SAM analysis
author: Narendra Solanki (NS)
last update: 17.08.2023 (NS)

This script takes preprocessed data and returns plots and statistical analysis as an RmD.
It can be run by itself, or used as an R child. 

INPUT DATA       : 
  Two Options:
    1. Do the preprocessing within this script:
                    Raw data (.xlsx file)
                    lookup.xlsx
    2. Use data that is already preprocessed
                    Preprocessed Raw data (.csv file)
             
CURRENT SETTINGS : 
                   
SECTIONS         :# 1.MANUAL ENTRIES
                    - In this section adjustments can be made regarding:
                        > Input files
                        > project name
                        > plots (color, theme etc.)
                        > enter the START DATE and TIME of the FIRST dark phase
                  
                  # 2. LOAD DATA:
                    - loads the data and lookup and tidies it up into a polished "data" data frame
                      2.1 Relabel individuals
                      2.2 Convert formats
                      2.3 Exclude NAs
                      2.4 Join lookup
                      2.5 Transform data and create new columns
                        >cage composition has to be manually adjusted according to the labbook if it is not in the lookup-file already
                  
                  # 3. Experimental settings
                    - Assess roughly the structure of the data (number of individuals in total, per cohort, per strain/treatment or genotype)
                  
                  # 4. Data Quality
                    - check for missing time points
                    - check for incomplete hours
                    - exclude data if necessary
                    
                  # 5. ANALYSIS
                    - Statistic Functions
                    - Results
                      - Total distance traveled and Mean distance traveled during dark and light phase
                      - Time series of distance traveled per hour and per phase
                        (For each section a plot and a statistical analysis is performed)
                  
                  # 6. Final conclusions and comments

NOTES             : 
- This script has been tested on the Project 'X'.
- The script can be adjusted to work with 2 or 3 treatment groups (or strains) and 1 or 2 cohorts (For an example of 3 groups and 2 cohorts see 'Y').
- If you work with already preprocessed data you won't need an extra lookup file and you won't need several preprocesssing steps within this script. Indicated sections should be out commented.
- This script is currently programmed to work with strains, but can be adjusted to work with treatments or genotypes easily:
    - In Experimental Conditions enter the correct names of data frames to display (e.g. replace 'list_of_strains' by 'list_of_genotypes') the necessary dataframes are created automatically.
    - For the statistic functions it is possible to give an argument ‘grouping factor’ which should be the name of the column containing the different strains, genotypes or treatments. 
    - In the plots the correct dataframes have to be selected manually. I recommend to do this using the search and replace function (ctrl + F) in Rstudio.

## SAM

__duration Test: 5 astronomical days and 5 bins of 24h__

Although it is called "social activity monitor", the only parameter currently available from this system is an individual index of distance traveled (total, across time (hours or phases of the day)).   

-- __Analysis of the data\:__ This setup gives an index of distance traveled by each (group housed) individual in the home cage over days of recording (total, per hour, per phase). The composition of the cage (mixed-treatment or same-treatment) need to be taken into account as a potential factor influencing the results. Non parametric tests and general linear mixed models can be used for statistical analysis. 

-- __Illustration\:__ Index of distance traveled per group and across hours (curve per group) or boxplots of (averaged) distance traveled per group across dark/light phases, day after day.

(each row in the preprocessed data represents an observation, i.e. the data for one individual for one hour. Hence we expect 24 observations per day per n of mice. Expected total number of observations = (24 * n of days + extra hours) * n of mice)

```{r strain_TOT_Dist_SAM, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height=4, fig.align="center"}

### Total distance traveled
pl_dis <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>% 
  #group by individual and calculate total_distance for each
  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender) %>%
  summarise(tot.dist = sum(distance.m)) %>%
  #create the plot environment/aesthetics
  ggplot(aes(x = PI, 
             y = tot.dist, 
             color = PI)) + 
  #add a boxplot
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +             #don't display outliers
  #add points shaped by cohort and not overlapping positions
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), jitter.width = 0.2, shape=1, size = 2) + #aes(shape = as.factor(genotype))
  #add 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #axis label and title
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "total distance traveled [m]", 
       title = "Total Distance - days (1-5)") + 
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() +
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

#pl_dis

### Mean distance traveled per phase 

# phase refers to light/dark phases. Here, light phase is from 6:00am to 6:00pm and dark phase vice versa.

#remove the first and last (incomplete) dark phases
sam_data_4gr_phase <- sam_data_4gr %>%
  filter(!(exp_day %in% c(1,5) & phase=="d"))
  
pl_dis_lightdark <- sam_data_4gr_phase %>%
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>% 
  group_by(Animal, genotype, phase, PI, gender) %>%
  summarise(avg_distance = mean(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = PI, 
             y = avg_distance, 
             color = PI, 
             )) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), jitter.width = 0.2, shape=1, size = 2) + 
  stat_n_text() +
  labs(
    x = "", 
    y = "mean distance [m]", 
    title = "Mean distance per phase - days (1-5)"
  ) + 
  #add a grid/columns by phase
  facet_grid(.~phase) +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) #+
  
#pl_dis_lightdark

#arrange the 2 plots created above into a grid with 2 rows and 1 column with automatic labelling (A,B)
Fig1 <- ggarrange(pl_dis, pl_dis_lightdark, labels="AUTO", ncol=2, nrow=1, common.legend=F, legend = "bottom")

#Fig1 <- ggarrange(pl_dis, pl_dis_lightdark, labels="AUTO", ncol=1, nrow=2, common.legend=F, legend = "bottom")

Fig1

```

__Figure 1 A - Total distance traveled (recorded over 5 experimental days), and B - Mean distance traveled during light phase (6am-6pm) and dark phase (6pm-6am) (recorded over 5 experimental days, first and last (incomplete) dark phases excluded)__  

__Statistics for Figure 1__

```{r stats_fig_1_A_SAM, echo=F}

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

#Fig_1A (COMPARISON BETWEEN GROUPS)

# perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
 st = tidy(pairwise.wilcox.test(pl_dis$data$tot.dist, pl_dis$data$PI, exact = FALSE, p.adjust.methods="BH")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",
           info = "Fig 1A total distance (m)",
         test = paste("between groups"), 
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

#Fig_1B (COMPARISON BETWEEN GROUPS)
# For the dark phase
data_d <- filter(pl_dis_lightdark$data, phase == "d")
# perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
 st = tidy(pairwise.wilcox.test(data_d$avg_distance, data_d$PI, exact = FALSE, p.adjust.methods="BH")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",
           info = "Fig 1B average distance (m) during dark phase",
         test = paste("between groups"), 
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
# For the light phase
data_l <- filter(pl_dis_lightdark$data, phase == "l")
# perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
 st = tidy(pairwise.wilcox.test(data_l$avg_distance, data_l$PI, exact = FALSE, p.adjust.methods="BH")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",
           info = "Fig 1B average distance (m) during light phase",
         test = paste("between groups"), 
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down"))

```

##### Time series of distance traveled for all 4-groups

```{r Dist_SAM, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 14, fig.align="center"}

### HOURLY data 
pl_hourly <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = h_from_start, y = distance.m, color = PI)) + 
    #create lines representing the mean in distance traveled for each group for each hour from start 
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               geom = "line", 
               aes(color = PI)) + 
  #add a ribbon to indicate standard deviation from the mean
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x), 
               fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x), 
               geom = "ribbon", 
               aes(fill = PI), 
               color = NA, 
               alpha = 0.15) + 
  # Annotations
  #create a sequence of rectangles spanning the indicated coordinates
  annotate("rect", xmin = c(seq(0, 108, 24)), 
           xmax = c(seq(0, 108, 24)+12), 
           ymin = -100, ymax = 300, alpha = 0.10) + 
  #create a sequence of text-labels with the specified content at the indicated x and y coordinates
  annotate("text", x = seq(12, (120), 24), y = 0, label = paste("Day",1:length(seq(12, (120), 24))), size = 4) + 
  #add a sequence of vertical lines at specified x-positions
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 120, 24), linetype = "dashed") +
  #add x-axis breaks/ticks and labels
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 120, 12), 
    #enter here start time of dark and light phase
    label = rep(c("18h", "6h"), 30)[1:length(seq(0, 120, 12))]
  ) + 
  # Labels etc
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "clock time", 
       y = "mean distance traveled per hour [m]", 
       title = "All days - 4gr_controls") + 
    #define y-limits
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-10, 225), expand=F)

#pl_hourly

### Data per phase
pl_per_day_per_phase <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  #group by individual
  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender, phase, exp_day) %>%
  summarise(distance = mean(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(phase),
             y = distance, 
             color = PI, 
             shape = PI)) +
  #create a rectangles shading dark and light phases
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.integer(factor(phase), levels = levels(as.factor(phase)), ordered = TRUE) - 0.5,
            xmax = as.integer(factor(phase), levels = levels(as.factor(phase)), ordered = TRUE) + 0.5,
            ymin = -Inf,
            ymax = Inf,
            fill =  phase, group = phase), color = NA, alpha = 0.3) +  # "color = NA" to remove border
  #custom gray and white color for dark and light phases
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("gray90", "white")) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge()) +
  #add a grid/columns by exp_day
  facet_grid(~exp_day) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("d" = "dark", "l" = "light")) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "mean distance traveled per phase [m]", title = "5 complete days") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank())

#pl_per_day_per_phase

### Data per day

  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender, exp_day) %>%
  summarise(distance = mean(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = as.factor(exp_day),
             y = distance, 
             color = PI, 
             shape = PI)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge()) +
  theme_classic() +

#pl_per_day

pl_mean_per_day_as_line <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  #group by individual
  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender, exp_day) %>%
  summarise(distance = mean(distance.m),
            sd = sd(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = as.factor(exp_day),
             y = distance,

        legend.title = element_blank())

#arrange the plots from this chunk and the 2 chunks above into a grid with 4 rows
Fig2 <- ggarrange(pl_hourly, pl_per_day_per_phase,pl_per_day,pl_mean_per_day_as_line, labels="AUTO", ncol=1, nrow=4, 
          common.legend=T, legend = "bottom")
```

**Figure 2. Time series of distance traveled per hour (A), per phase (B), per experimental day (C) and connected means per experimental day (D).**  
For all plots an experimental day starts at 06:00 and ends at 18:00.        
Note A: Grey areas represent dark phases and white areas represent light phases.
Note B, C & D: The days depicted here represent the experimental days as indicated in A. Day 1 starts at 06:00 and day 5 ends at 18:00. Data after Day 5 is excluded. B depicts the phases (dark, light), whereas C and D only depict whole days.
Note D: means and SD per groups per day.

**Statistics (MCMCglmm) for Figure 2**  

MCMCglmm was used to check the influence of the following variables on the distance traveled: PI/groups, phase, hour from start (treated as fixed variables), and id (treated as a random variable).  

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}

# For a detailed description of the MCMCglmm, see 20190423_GLMM_Vladi.pdf in 
# Z:\AOCF-Test_apparatus information_analysis\Data analysis\data_analyst_EDM\Documentation\Vladi

prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig2_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c(list_of_PIs)),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  

m <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ PI + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(fig2_data), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(m)


# plot(m)
# The plots can be interpreted as follows. If the trace (on the left) is a nice
# caterpillar, we can say the model converged and we can say something about the
# results. The density plot is the density of the values in the trace. If the 
# density is a nice bell shape (Gaussian-like) and the value 0 is outside of the 
# density, we can say there is an effect. 

# Fixed effect interpretation:
# The intercept is in this case the effect of HOM/dark phase. The other plots are
# deviations from HOM/dark. So there is no effect of genotype wt (0 is in
# the density plot).
# There is an effect of light vs dark and an effect of hours from start. 
# There is also an effect of time point. 

# Random effects interpretation:
# There is an effect of id, so there is an effect simply because the animals are 
# different animals. 
# Units means any other hidden effects that explain the model. These do not depend on 
# our data and are generally not discussed.

# Be aware that this technique requires Gaussian data and the data is not
# completely Gaussian. There are ways to transform the data, but as most of the 
# model had a good fit on the data, I do not think it is necessary. -EdM

# https://ourcodingclub.github.io/2018/01/22/mcmcglmm.html
```
The intercept is in this case the effect of "group gr1/dark phase". The other plots are deviations from gr1/dark phase. So here there is an effect of group and an effect of hours from start.

__Statistics for Figure 3__

```{r stats_fig_1_A_SAM_gender, echo=F}

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

#Fig_3A (COMPARISON BETWEEN GENDERS WITHIN GROUPS)

pl_dist3 <- pl_dis3$data %>%
  #convert strain and cohort into factors 
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c(list_of_PIs)),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))

for (i in 1:length(list_of_PIs)) {
  stat_data3 <- pl_dist3 %>%
    filter(PI == list_of_PIs[i])
     # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between genders within group
   st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data3$tot.dist ~ stat_data3$gender, exact = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Rank Sum",
           info = "Fig 3A total distance (m)",
           test = paste("between genders for", list_of_PIs[i]), 
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

#Fig_3B (COMPARISON BETWEEN GENDERS WITHIN GROUPS)

data_d3 <- filter(pl_dis_lightdark3$data, phase == "d") %>%
```

**Statistics (MCMCglmm) for Figure 4**  

MCMCglmm was used to check the influence of the following variables on the distance traveled: gender, phase, hour from start (treated as fixed variables), and id (treated as a random variable).  

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM_gender, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}

prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig4_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c(list_of_PIs)),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  
stat_fig4 = tibble()

for (i in 1:length(list_of_PIs)) {
  stat_data4 <- fig4_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(PI == list_of_PIs[i])
  
  st_x = tibble(res_group = list_of_PIs[i], effect = c("(Intercept)", "gendermale", "phasel", "h_from_start"))
  
mcmc <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ gender + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(stat_data4), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(mcmc)

    x <- summary(mcmc)$solutions
    x <- data.frame(x) #%>%      mutate(tp = m)
    
    x$effect <- rownames(x)
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    
    st_x <- full_join(st_x, x, by = "effect") %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(pMCMC < 0.05, "*", ""))
    
    stat_fig4 <- bind_rows(stat_fig4, st_x)
  }

stat_fig4 %>%
  #dplyr::select(-alternative) %>%
  kable( longtable=TRUE) %>% #removed booktabs = T, otherwise "repeat_header" doesn't work
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down","repeat_header"))

```

The intercept is in this case the effect of "genderfemale/dark phase and hour from start". The other plots are deviations from genderfemale/dark phase.

```{r Dist_SAM_gender_comb1, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 14, fig.align="center"}
### HOURLY data 
pl_hourly6 <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = h_from_start, y = distance.m, linetype = gender, color = gender)) + 
  #create lines representing the mean in distance traveled for each group for each hour from start 
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               geom = "line", 
               aes(color = gender)) + 
  #add a ribbon to indicate standard deviation from the mean
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x), 
               fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x), 
               geom = "ribbon", 
               aes(fill = gender), 
               color = NA, 
               alpha = 0.15) + 
  # Annotations
  #create a sequence of rectangles spanning the indicated coordinates
  annotate("rect", xmin = c(seq(0, 108, 24)), 
           xmax = c(seq(0, 108, 24)+12), 
           ymin = -100, ymax = 300, alpha = 0.10) + 
  #create a sequence of text-labels with the specified content at the indicated x and y coordinates
  annotate("text", x = seq(12, (120), 24), y = 0, label = paste("Day",1:length(seq(12, (120), 24))), size = 4) + 
  #add a sequence of vertical lines at specified x-positions
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 120, 24), linetype = "dashed") +
  #add x-axis breaks/ticks and labels
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 120, 12), 
    #enter here start time of dark and light phase
    label = rep(c("18h", "6h"), 30)[1:length(seq(0, 120, 12))]
  ) + 
  # Labels etc
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "clock time", 
       y = "mean distance traveled per hour [m]", 
       title = "All days - 4gr_controls") + 
    #define y-limits
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-10, 225), expand=F)
```

**Statistics (MCMCglmm) for Figure 6**  

MCMCglmm was used to check the influence of the following variables on the distance traveled: gender, phase, hour from start (treated as fixed variables), and id (treated as a random variable).  

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM_gender_comb1, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}

prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig6_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c(list_of_PIs)),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  
stat_fig6 = tibble()

#for (i in 1:length(list_of_PIs)) {
  stat_data6 <- fig6_data #%>%
 #   dplyr::filter(PI == list_of_PIs[i])
  
  st_x = tibble(res_group = "all gr combined", effect = c("(Intercept)", "gendermale", "phasel", "h_from_start"))
  
mcmc <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ gender + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(stat_data6), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(mcmc)

    x <- summary(mcmc)$solutions
    x <- data.frame(x) #%>%      mutate(tp = m)
    
    x$effect <- rownames(x)
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    
    st_x <- full_join(st_x, x, by = "effect") %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(pMCMC < 0.05, "*", ""))
    
    stat_fig6 <- bind_rows(stat_fig6, st_x)
#  }

stat_fig6 %>%
  #dplyr::select(-alternative) %>%
  kable( longtable=TRUE) %>% #removed booktabs = T, otherwise "repeat_header" doesn't work
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down","repeat_header"))

```

The intercept is in this case the effect of "genderfemale/dark phase and hour from start". The other plots are deviations from genderfemale/dark phase.

```{r strain_TOT_Dist_SAM_gender_comb2, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height=4, fig.align="center"}
  
### Total distance traveled
pl_dis7 <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2", "gr3", "gr4"),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  #group by individual and calculate total_distance for each
  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender) %>%
  summarise(tot.dist = sum(distance.m)) %>%
  #create the plot environment/aesthetics
  ggplot(aes(x = "", 
             y = tot.dist, 
             color = gender)) + 
  #add a boxplot
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +             #don't display outliers
  #add points shaped by cohort and not overlapping positions
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), jitter.width = 0.2, shape=1, size = 2) + #aes(shape = as.factor(genotype))
  #add 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #axis label and title
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "total distance traveled [m]", 
       title = "Total Distance - days (1-5)") + 
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() +
    #add text 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #count n of each gender and add it to the plot
  geom_text(aes(label=..count.., y = ..count..), stat="count", position = position_dodge(width = 0.95), size=3, vjust = +2) +
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

#pl_dis7

  filter(!(exp_day %in% c(1,5) & phase=="d"))
  
pl_dis_lightdark7 <- sam_data_4gr_phase %>%
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2", "gr3", "gr4"),
         genotype == "WT") %>% 
  group_by(Animal, genotype, phase, PI, gender) %>%
  summarise(avg_distance = mean(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", 
             y = avg_distance, 
             color = gender, 
             )) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), jitter.width = 0.2, shape=1, size = 2) + 
  stat_n_text() +
  labs(
    x = "", 
    y = "mean distance [m]", 
    title = "Mean distance per phase - days (1-5)"
  ) + 
  #add a grid/columns by phase
  facet_grid(.~phase) +
  theme_pubr() +
    #add text 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #count n of each gender and add it to the plot
  geom_text(aes(label=..count.., y = ..count..), stat="count", position = position_dodge(width = 0.95), size=3, vjust = +3) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) #+
```

```{r strain_TOT_Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height=4, fig.align="center"}
  #add a boxplot
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +             #don't display outliers
  #add points shaped by cohort and not overlapping positions
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), jitter.width = 0.2, shape=1, size = 2) + #aes(shape = as.factor(genotype))
  #add 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #axis label and title
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "total distance traveled [m]", 
       title = "Total Distance - days (1-5)") + 
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() +
    #add text 'n='
  stat_n_text() +
  #count n of each gender and add it to the plot
  geom_text(aes(label=..count.., y = ..count..), stat="count", position = position_dodge(width = 0.95), size=3, vjust = +2) +
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))
```

##### Time series of distance traveled gender wise for group-2

```{r Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 14, fig.align="center"}

### HOURLY data 
pl_hourly10 <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2"),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = h_from_start, y = distance.m, linetype = gender, color = gender)) + 
  #create lines representing the mean in distance traveled for each group for each hour from start 
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               geom = "line", 
               aes(color = gender)) + 
  #add a ribbon to indicate standard deviation from the mean
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x), 
               fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x), 
               geom = "ribbon", 
               aes(fill = gender), 
               color = NA, 
               alpha = 0.15) + 
  # Annotations
  #create a sequence of rectangles spanning the indicated coordinates
  annotate("rect", xmin = c(seq(0, 108, 24)), 
           xmax = c(seq(0, 108, 24)+12), 
           ymin = -100, ymax = 300, alpha = 0.10) + 
  #create a sequence of text-labels with the specified content at the indicated x and y coordinates
  annotate("text", x = seq(12, (120), 24), y = 0, label = paste("Day",1:length(seq(12, (120), 24))), size = 4) + 
  #add a sequence of vertical lines at specified x-positions
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 120, 24), linetype = "dashed") +
  #add x-axis breaks/ticks and labels
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 120, 12), 
    #enter here start time of dark and light phase
    label = rep(c("18h", "6h"), 30)[1:length(seq(0, 120, 12))]
  ) + 
  # Labels etc
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "clock time", 
       y = "mean distance traveled per hour [m]", 
       title = "All days - gr2_control") + 
    #define y-limits
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-10, 225), expand=F)

### Data per phase
pl_per_day_per_phase10 <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2"),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  #group by individual
  group_by(Animal, genotype, PI, gender, phase, exp_day) %>%
  summarise(distance = mean(distance.m)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(phase),
             y = distance, 
             color = gender)) +
  #create a rectangles shading dark and light phases
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = as.integer(factor(phase), levels = levels(as.factor(phase)), ordered = TRUE) - 0.5,
            xmax = as.integer(factor(phase), levels = levels(as.factor(phase)), ordered = TRUE) + 0.5,
            ymin = -Inf,
            ymax = Inf,
            fill =  phase, group = phase), color = NA, alpha = 0.3) +  # "color = NA" to remove border
  #custom gray and white color for dark and light phases
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("gray90", "white")) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge()) +
  #add a grid/columns by exp_day
  facet_grid(~exp_day) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("d" = "dark", "l" = "light")) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "mean distance traveled per phase [m]", title = "5 complete days") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank())
```

**Figure 10. Time series of distance traveled per hour (A), per phase (B), per experimental day (C) and connected means per experimental day (D) gender wise.**  
For all plots an experimental day starts at 06:00 and ends at 18:00.        
Note A: Grey areas represent dark phases and white areas represent light phases.
Note B, C & D: The days depicted here represent the experimental days as indicated in A. Day 1 starts at 06:00 and day 5 ends at 18:00. Data after Day 5 is excluded. B depicts the phases (dark, light), whereas C and D only depict whole days.
Note D: means and SD per groups per day.

**Statistics (MCMCglmm) for Figure 10**  

MCMCglmm was used to check the influence of the following variables on the distance traveled: gender, phase, hour from start (treated as fixed variables), and id (treated as a random variable).  

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}

prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig10_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2"),
         genotype == "WT") %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  
stat_fig10 = tibble()

#for (i in 1:length(list_of_PIs)) {
  stat_data10 <- fig10_data #%>%
 #   dplyr::filter(PI == list_of_PIs[i])
  
  st_x = tibble(res_group = "gr2_control", effect = c("(Intercept)", "gendermale", "phasel", "h_from_start"))
  
mcmc <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ gender + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(stat_data10), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(mcmc)

    x <- summary(mcmc)$solutions
    x <- data.frame(x) #%>%      mutate(tp = m)
    
    x$effect <- rownames(x)
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    
    st_x <- full_join(st_x, x, by = "effect") %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(pMCMC < 0.05, "*", ""))
    
    stat_fig10 <- bind_rows(stat_fig10, st_x)
#  }

stat_fig10 %>%
  #dplyr::select(-alternative) %>%
  kable( longtable=TRUE) %>% #removed booktabs = T, otherwise "repeat_header" doesn't work
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down","repeat_header"))

```

The intercept is in this case the effect of "genderfemale/dark phase and hour from start". The other plots are deviations from genderfemale/dark phase.

**Statistics (MCMCglmm) for Figure 12**  

MCMCglmm was used to check the influence of the following variables on the distance traveled: gender, phase, hour from start (treated as fixed variables), and id (treated as a random variable).  

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_mut, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}

prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig12_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2"),
         genotype == "KO") %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  
stat_fig12 = tibble()

#for (i in 1:length(list_of_PIs)) {
  stat_data12 <- fig12_data #%>%
 #   dplyr::filter(PI == list_of_PIs[i])
  
  st_x = tibble(res_group = "gr2_mutant", effect = c("(Intercept)", "gendermale", "phasel", "h_from_start"))
  
mcmc <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ gender + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(stat_data12), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(mcmc)

    x <- summary(mcmc)$solutions
    x <- data.frame(x) #%>%      mutate(tp = m)
    
    x$effect <- rownames(x)
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    
    st_x <- full_join(st_x, x, by = "effect") %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(pMCMC < 0.05, "*", ""))
    
    stat_fig12 <- bind_rows(stat_fig12, st_x)
#  }

stat_fig12 %>%
  #dplyr::select(-alternative) %>%
  kable( longtable=TRUE) %>% #removed booktabs = T, otherwise "repeat_header" doesn't work
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down","repeat_header"))

```

The intercept is in this case the effect of "genderfemale/dark phase and hour from start". The other plots are deviations from genderfemale/dark phase.

```{r strain_TOT_Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control_mut, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height=4, fig.align="center"}
### Total distance traveled
```

__Statistics (Between genders) for Figure 13__

```{r stats_fig_1_A_SAM_gender_gr2_control_mut_gn, echo=F}

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

#Fig_5A (COMPARISON BETWEEN GENDERS)

pl_dist13 <- pl_dis13$data %>%
  #convert strain and cohort into factors 
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)),
         genotype=factor(genotype, levels = c(list_of_genotypes_pigv)))

for (i in 1:length(list_of_genotypes_pigv)) {
  stat_data13 <- pl_dist13 %>%
    filter(genotype == list_of_genotypes_pigv[i])
     # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between genders within group
   st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data13$tot.dist ~ stat_data13$gender, exact = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Rank Sum",
           info = "Fig 13A total distance (m)",
           test = paste("between genders for gr2", list_of_genotypes_pigv[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

#Fig_5B (COMPARISON BETWEEN GENDERS)
# For the dark phase
data_d13 <- filter(pl_dis_lightdark13$data, phase == "d") %>%
  #convert strain and cohort into factors 
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)),
         genotype=factor(genotype, levels = c(list_of_genotypes_pigv)))

for (i in 1:length(list_of_genotypes_pigv)) {
  stat_data13d <- data_d13 %>%
    filter(genotype == list_of_genotypes_pigv[i])
     # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between genders within group
   st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data13d$avg_distance ~ stat_data13d$gender, exact = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Rank Sum",
           info = "Fig 13B average distance (m) during dark phase",
           test = paste("between genders for gr2", list_of_genotypes_pigv[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

# For the light phase
data_l13 <- filter(pl_dis_lightdark13$data, phase == "l") %>%
  #convert strain and cohort into factors 
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)),
         genotype=factor(genotype, levels = c(list_of_genotypes_pigv)))

for (i in 1:length(list_of_genotypes_pigv)) {
  stat_data13l <- data_l13 %>%
    filter(genotype == list_of_genotypes_pigv[i])
     # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between genders within group
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data13l$avg_distance ~ stat_data13l$gender, exact = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Rank Sum",
           info = "Fig 13B average distance (m) during light phase",
           test = paste("between genders for gr2", list_of_genotypes_pigv[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
   #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down"))
```

```{r Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control_mut, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 14, fig.align="center"}
  #create lines representing the mean in distance traveled for each group for each hour from start 
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               geom = "line", 
               aes(color = gender)) + 
  #add a ribbon to indicate standard deviation from the mean
  stat_summary(fun = mean, 
               fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x), 
               fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x), 
               geom = "ribbon", 
               aes(fill = gender), 
               color = NA, 
               alpha = 0.15) + 
  # Annotations
  #create a sequence of rectangles spanning the indicated coordinates
  annotate("rect", xmin = c(seq(0, 108, 24)), 
           xmax = c(seq(0, 108, 24)+12), 
           ymin = -100, ymax = 300, alpha = 0.10) + 
  #create a sequence of text-labels with the specified content at the indicated x and y coordinates
  annotate("text", x = seq(12, (120), 24), y = 0, label = paste("Day",1:length(seq(12, (120), 24))), size = 4) + 
  #add a sequence of vertical lines at specified x-positions
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 120, 24), linetype = "dashed") +
  #add x-axis breaks/ticks and labels
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 120, 12), 
    #enter here start time of dark and light phase
    label = rep(c("18h", "6h"), 30)[1:length(seq(0, 120, 12))]
  ) + 
  # Labels etc
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "clock time", 
       y = "mean distance traveled per hour [m]", 
       title = "All days - gr2_control_&_mutant") +

  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-10, 225), expand=F)
```

```{r MCMCglmm_Hourly_Dist_SAM_gender_gr2_control_mut_ge, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 15, echo=F, warnings=F}
prior <- list(R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002), G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)))

fig14_data <- sam_data_4gr %>%  
  #enter the experimental days you want to display in the plot
  filter(exp_day %in% c(1,2,3,4,5),
         PI %in% c("gr2")) %>%
  mutate(PI=factor(PI, levels = c("gr2")),
         gender=factor(gender, levels = c(list_of_genders)))
  
stat_fig15 = tibble()

for (i in 1:length(list_of_genders)) {
  stat_data15 <- fig14_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(gender == list_of_genders[i])
  
  st_x = tibble(gender = list_of_genders[i], effect = c("(Intercept)", "genotypeWT", "phasel", "h_from_start"))
  
mcmc <- MCMCglmm(distance.m ~ genotype + phase + h_from_start, 
              random = ~ Animal, 
              data = data.frame(stat_data15), 
              family = "gaussian", 
              prior = prior,
              verbose = FALSE)

summary(mcmc)

    x <- summary(mcmc)$solutions
    x <- data.frame(x) #%>%      mutate(tp = m)
    
    x$effect <- rownames(x)
    rownames(x) <- NULL
    
    st_x <- full_join(st_x, x, by = "effect") %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(pMCMC < 0.05, "*", ""))
    
    stat_fig15 <- bind_rows(stat_fig15, st_x)
  }

stat_fig15 %>%
  #dplyr::select(-alternative) %>%
  kable( longtable=TRUE) %>% #removed booktabs = T, otherwise "repeat_header" doesn't work
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down","repeat_header"))

```

The intercept is in this case the effect of "genderfemale/dark phase and hour from start". The other plots are deviations from genderfemale/dark phase.
